title: States of Matter
text: Matter commonly exists in four states: solid, liquid, gas, and plasma. In solids, particles are tightly packed in a fixed structure. In liquids, particles are close but can move past each other, allowing flow. In gases, particles are widely spaced and move freely. Plasma, the most abundant state in the universe, consists of ionized gas with free-moving charged particles, found in stars and lightning. Transitions between states occur through changes in temperature and pressure (melting, freezing, boiling, condensation, sublimation).
